segments: 284 The lord of Melitene, the Caliph sent a golden collar for his neck,
a sign of vassalage,
and a golden sceptre,
and four black banners, and drums to be beaten before him.
And he was proclaimed Malik Ghazi.
And when the envoys arrived, they found that he was sick,
and after a few days he died.
Then they invested his son Muhammad,
and departed.
Now this Malik Muhammad,
Caesarea of Cappadocia,
which had long been in ruins,
restored,
and he resided there.
And he came to Melitene,
because he was afraid that they might assist his brother;
and he took with him as hostages the children of the nobles, and departed.
He encountered his brother Yaghan and killed him.
Dawlat, however, his other brother, pillaged the territory of Melitene.
And in the seventh month of this year, the Caliph abolished the proclamation of Sultan Mas'ud,
and gathered forces of seven thousand to wage war with him,
because he heard that he had only one thousand five hundred with him.
Then there were five thousand with the Caliph,
and with Mas'ud fifteen thousand.
And they met each other,
and the Caliph's side was broken,
and the Caliph al-Mustarshid himself was captured.
And the treasury that was with him was plundered:
there were seventy mule-loads of gold and silver with him,
and five thousand camel-loads,
and four hundred mule-loads of baggage, clothes, and traveling equipment.
It is said
that there were with him more than forty thousand caps, turbans, and sewn tunics of fine cloth {OCR?}.
Now Mas'ud commanded heralds to proclaim:
"The goods and all the wealth are yours,
but the blood is mine.
And whoever kills a man,
I will kill him in his place."
Therefore, except for five persons, no one was killed.
And it was proclaimed again:
"Whoever remains here of the followers of the Caliph's faction,
I will surely kill him."
Then the Baghdadis crowded each other, and being stripped and naked,
they fled to the right and to the left.
And Sultan Mas'ud sent a governor (shiḥnah) to Baghdad,
and told the Caliph to write with him a letter to Baghdad of acknowledgment,
and that he was in great honor with Mas'ud,
and behold, he would come to them soon.
Now when the governor went and brought the letter,
the Baghdadis knew that he had written it against his will,
